text_blocks.snippet: Blood pressure of 130/80 mm Hg or higher is considered high blood pressure (hypertension).
Readings use two numbers: the top number (systolic) and the bottom number (diastolic).

list.snippet: Normal: Less than 120 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic.
Elevated: 120–129 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic.
Stage 1 Hypertension: 130–139 mm Hg systolic or 80–89 mm Hg diastolic.
Stage 2 Hypertension: 140 mm Hg or higher systolic or 90 mm Hg or higher diastolic.
Hypertensive Crisis: Higher than 180 mm Hg systolic and/or higher than 120 mm Hg diastolic. Readings this high require immediate medical care.

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more about these categories from the American Heart Association.
